definitions.gloss: koban; oval gold coin of the Edo period
definitions.explanation: A flat, oval gold coin used as currency in Japan during the Edo period (1603–1868), and a familiar symbol of old wealth.

examples.japanese: {時代劇|じだいげき}に{小判|こばん}の{詰|つ}まった{箱|はこ}が{出|で}てきた。
examples.english: A box stuffed with koban appeared in the period drama.

examples.japanese: {江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}には、{小判|こばん}{一枚|いちまい}でかなりの{価値|かち}があったと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: In the Edo period, a single koban is said to have been worth a considerable amount.

notes:
An oval gold coin of the Edo period and a familiar emblem of historical wealth in Japan. It appears constantly in period dramas and folktales.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {小判|こばん}{型|がた}: koban-shaped (oval)
- {大判|おおばん}{小判|こばん}: large and small gold coins (great riches)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {猫|ねこ}に{小判|こばん}: 'a koban to a cat' — casting pearls before swine; giving something valuable to someone who cannot appreciate it.
